A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renaming, reformatting, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-Neo unlearning experiments on TDEC, including downstream performance, computational cost, and rank and module ablations in Table 1 and Figures 2–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds TOFU evaluations in Section 4.3 and continual-unlearning results in Appendix D.1.

M1.justification: The inverted hinge loss, relative-Fisher weighting, low-rank initialization, base-weight compensation, and retain-set regularization remain the same. FLoRA is renamed FILA; the new evaluations do not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on TOFU author-profile question answering, including retention tests on real authors and world facts. Appendix D.1 also introduces sequential TDEC deletion requests. These extend coverage beyond v1's single-stage TDEC experiments; the original reasoning and dialogue datasets remain.

E2.justification: GA and GD remain the evaluated unlearning baselines. The new TOFU comparisons additionally include retain-set-only finetuned reference models, explicitly plotted in Figure 5. Newly discussed methods requiring auxiliary models or full training data are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: TOFU introduces Phi-1.5B and Llama2-7B experiments, 1%/5%/10% deletion splits, reference-model comparisons, Forget Quality and Model Utility metrics, and five-epoch tuning protocols. Appendix D.1 adds four sequential tasks. TDEC's learning-rate description also changes from separate full-tuning and LoRA rates to a stated fixed 2e-4, without establishing that the retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a four-task continual-unlearning test of cumulative capability retention. Section 4.3 examines TOFU behavior across deletion fractions, adapter ranks, and epochs, including excessive unlearning. The existing rank and target-module ablations remain.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported number of TDEC forget sets from three to five, although the retained results do not establish additional runs. TOFU introduces Kolmogorov-Smirnov p-values for distributional comparison; these are evaluation statistics rather than uncertainty intervals for mean performance.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the plotted results in Figures 2–4 are unchanged. v2 adds substantial TOFU and continual-unlearning results in Figures 5–6, including better utility retention with IHL, faster forgetting with FILA in many settings, and excessive unlearning in some TOFU configurations. These are new findings, not improvements to the original same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 removes v1's sign-inconsistent equality identifying the negative log-likelihood loss gradient with the positive log-probability gradient. The IHL derivative formulas, Fisher-weighted approximation, and mathematical material in Appendices A–B otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions present the same two central contributions and claim efficient, stable unlearning with better preservation of retained capabilities. The added TOFU evidence broadens support for these claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limits to the robustness narrative: FILA can cause excessive unlearning, and choosing a stopping point is difficult without an oracle reference model. It interprets this behavior through the Streisand effect and discusses reference-free evaluation as future work. It also removes v1's suggestion that merging adapters provides security by concealing unlearning history.

D1.justification: v2 supplies TOFU learning rates, epoch counts, batch size, and AdamW optimizer information, and newly specifies rank 32 for the existing module ablation. Hardware disclosure changes from 16 A100 GPUs on GCP to A100 40GB GPUs without the count or provider. Moving the retained evaluation-dataset list to Appendix C adds no new implementation information.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of Liu et al.'s two-stage unlearning method, references Llama 3 and AdamW, and clarifies its positioning against approaches requiring auxiliary models or full training data. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for works already cited.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial portions of the method and results prose are rewritten. FLoRA becomes FILA, the experimental narrative is expanded and reorganized, and dataset descriptions move to a new experimental-details appendix.

P2.justification: v2 adds the extensive multipanel TOFU display in Figure 5 and the continual-unlearning plots in Figure 6. Existing figures are resized and repositioned, captions are revised, and Table 1 is reformatted. The retained plots display the same results despite their changed dimensions and tick layouts.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's small TDEC deletion sets by testing structured author-profile removal on additional model families and cumulative effects of sequential deletion. It also identifies excessive unlearning and reference-dependent stopping, making the practical limitations more informative. These gains address important gaps in the original evidence and outweigh the remaining ambiguity about TDEC setting changes and whether retained results were rerun.
